toc.title: Layers of protection: what protects what
RLS group membership and sensitivity labels

html:
1Layers of protection: what protects what

Power BI security works in layers, and each layer protects a different thing. Many exam questions ask which layer fits. Read the requirement first, then name the layer, then pick the setting. One scenario can need two layers, for example row-level security for the rows and a sensitivity label for the exported file.

Layer What it protects Where you set it Who it applies to
Row-level security (RLS) Rows of a semantic model Roles in Desktop; members in the service Viewers only
Object-level security (OLS) Columns and tables Roles in the semantic model Members of the role
Workspace role Every item in the workspace The workspace access list Users or groups
Item permission One item Sharing or permissions of that item The people it is given to
Sensitivity label The content and its exports Desktop or the service The labeled item and its downloads
Exam tip

. RLS limits rows, OLS limits columns and tables, a role or permission decides what a person can do, and a label protects the file when it leaves. Match the layer to the verb in the question.

2Workspace roles and item-level access

Role What it can do Key limit
Admin Everything: delete the workspace, add or remove anyone, let Contributors update the app None
Member Add lower roles only, publish or update the app, share, edit content Cannot delete the workspace
Contributor Create, edit and delete content; schedule refresh Cannot publish an app (can update it only if an Admin allows)
Viewer View and interact only The only role RLS applies to

Roles can be given to users or to groups.

Item-level access is sharing one item. Sharing an item gives Read by default. The person gets that item only, not a place in the workspace. A workspace role reaches every item in the workspace; an item permission reaches one.

Exam tip

. A Contributor cannot publish an app, and only a Viewer is restricted by RLS. A Member can publish the app but cannot delete the workspace.

3Access to semantic models

Permission What it allows
Read Interact with reports built on the model
Build Create new content from the model, Analyze in Excel, see hidden fields, export underlying data
Reshare Give others access to the model
Write Edit and republish the model

A workspace role brings these implicitly:

Workspace role Permissions on the model
Admin, Member Read, Build, Reshare and Write
Contributor Read, Build and Write
Viewer Read only

Sharing gives Read by default. Build and Reshare are granted on purpose. Only the owner can change the scheduled refresh and credentials.

Exam tip

. Build lets people create new reports from a shared model; Read does not. A Viewer has Read only, so a Viewer needs Build granted to use Analyze in Excel.

4Row-level security roles

RLS limits which rows a person sees. The steps are:

  1. In Desktop, on the Modeling tab, choose Manage roles. Create a role, pick a table and write a DAX filter.
  2. Test it with View as in Desktop or Test as role in the service.
  3. Publish, then add members in the service (section 5).

A static filter uses a fixed value, so you need one role per value. A dynamic filter uses USERPRINCIPALNAME, which returns the signed-in user's name, so one role serves everyone.

// Static role "West" on the Store table
Store[Region] = "West"

// Dynamic role "Reps" on the Customer table
Customer[Email] = USERPRINCIPALNAME()
RLS rule Detail
Additive A user in two roles sees the union of their rows
Who is limited Viewers only, including Viewers with Build
Not limited Admin, Member and Contributor (anyone with Write permission)
Scope Rows only; OLS covers columns and tables
Sources DirectQuery is supported
Exam tip

. Define the role in Desktop, assign members in the service. If a Contributor still sees every row, RLS is not applied to that role.

5RLS group membership and sensitivity labels

Add members in the service: open the semantic model, then Security, choose the role and add users or groups.

Member type Supported?
Security groups Yes
Mail-enabled groups and distribution groups Yes
Microsoft 365 groups No
Service principals No

Sensitivity labels come from Microsoft Purview Information Protection.

Label fact Detail
Apply in Desktop (the Sensitivity button) and the service
Items Semantic models, reports, dashboards, dataflows, paginated reports
Requirements Pro or PPU, and membership of a security group allowed to apply labels
What it does Does not control access in the service; it applies protection (encryption) on export to Excel, PowerPoint, PDF and .pbix download
Inheritance New content inherits a label, and downstream content inherits too
Other The more restrictive label wins on .pbix download; subscription attachments are protected
Exam tip

. Microsoft 365 groups are not supported for RLS membership; use a security group. A sensitivity label protects exports, it does not block viewing in the service.

6Exam Q&A

6.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1A colleague must publish the workspace app and add people as Contributors, but must not be able to delete the workspace. Which role should the colleague get?

  • AMember role on the workspace
  • BAdmin role on the workspace
  • CContributor role on the workspace
  • DViewer role on the workspace
Show the answer

Answer: A. A Member can publish the app and add lower roles but cannot delete the workspace, while an Admin can delete it and a Contributor cannot publish an app.

S2An RLS role limits each sales region to its own rows. A user who is a workspace Contributor and is also assigned to a role still sees every row. What explains this?

  • AThe filter must be rewritten to use USERPRINCIPALNAME
  • BRLS is applied only to users with the Viewer role
  • CThe role needs the Reshare permission to be added
  • DRLS is ignored for semantic models in Import mode
Show the answer

Answer: B. RLS is not applied to Admin, Member or Contributor, because they have Write permission on the model.

S3Each sales rep must see only their own customers, and the Customer table has an Email column. There are 300 reps. What is the best design?

  • AA static role for each rep with a fixed email value
  • BA workspace Viewer role for each rep on the report
  • CA dynamic role that compares Email with the signed-in user
  • DA sensitivity label for each rep on the customer data
Show the answer

Answer: C. One dynamic role with USERPRINCIPALNAME serves every rep, while static roles would need 300 roles.

S4An admin wants to add a whole team to an RLS role by using one group in the service. Which group can be added?

  • AA Microsoft 365 group of the team members
  • BA security group of the team members
  • CA service principal for the team members
  • DA workspace app audience of team members
Show the answer

Answer: B. Security groups are supported for RLS membership, while Microsoft 365 groups and service principals are not.

S5A user must build new reports from a shared semantic model but must not change or republish it. Which permission should the user get on the model?

  • ARead permission on the semantic model
  • BReshare permission on the semantic model
  • CWrite permission on the semantic model
  • DBuild permission on the semantic model
Show the answer

Answer: D. Build allows creating new content from the model, while Write would allow editing and republishing it.

S6A report labeled Confidential is exported to PowerPoint by an analyst. What happens?

  • AThe exported file keeps the label and its protection
  • BThe label is dropped, so the exported file is unprotected
  • CThe export is blocked for every user who has that label
  • DThe analyst must apply a new label before saving the file
Show the answer

Answer: A. Sensitivity labels apply protection to exports such as Excel, PowerPoint and PDF files.

6.2 Recall questions

R1Which workspace role can delete the workspace?

Show the answer

Admin.

R2Which role is the only one that RLS restricts?

Show the answer

Viewer.

R3Where do you define RLS roles, and where do you add members?

Show the answer

Roles in Desktop on the Modeling tab; members in the service under the model's Security.

R4Which DAX function returns the signed-in user's name for dynamic RLS?

Show the answer

USERPRINCIPALNAME.

R5What access does sharing an item give by default?

Show the answer

Read.

R6Which security hides columns and tables rather than rows?

Show the answer

Object-level security.

7Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
What protects what RLS rows; OLS columns and tables; workspace role all items; item permission one item; label protects exports
Workspace roles Admin everything; Member adds lower roles and publishes the app; Contributor edits but no app publishing; Viewer view only
Item-level access sharing gives Read by default; item permission is narrower than a role
Model permissions Read, Build, Reshare, Write; Admin and Member all four; Contributor three; Viewer Read
RLS roles Desktop, Modeling, Manage roles; static or dynamic with USERPRINCIPALNAME; additive; Viewers only; View as or Test as role
RLS membership service, model, Security; security, mail-enabled and distribution groups yes; Microsoft 365 groups and service principals no
Sensitivity labels Microsoft Purview Information Protection; Desktop and service; Pro or PPU; encrypt on export; inheritance
